summary: Ephemeral WIF->AWS debug role failing for private deploys; need timebound debug-proxy role and docs
description: Issue summary: Oncall runbook execution for private deployments hit a blocker when our ephemeral Workload Identity Federation (WIF) -> AWS debug proxy fails to assume the target AWS role. Impact: SREs cannot access customer-dedicated resources (S3 + KMS) to complete a live debug, delaying incident resolution for a Dedicated onboarding automation failure. This ticket requests a timebound, minimally scoped debug-proxy IAM role in target prod account(s), plus a short runbook update describing correct audience and token parameters for WIF->AWS chaining.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From GKE pod with workload identity enabled, call STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity using the token from metadata server
2) Observe 400/InvalidIdentityToken from AWS STS in logs
3) When forcing a successful STS call using a manually minted token with audience=sts.amazonaws.com, the role assumption succeeds but KMS:Decrypt is denied for the assumed role
4) Attempt to decrypt an envelope key with aws kms decrypt -> AccessDenied
5) Reproduce occurs only for private-deploy worker accounts in eu-west and not in self-service staging accounts.
logs: AWS STS response: {"Error":{"Code":"InvalidIdentityToken","Message":"STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity failed due to token audience mismatch"}}
Cloud Audit (GCP): Token issued with aud="https://iam.googleapis.com/" and sub="system:serviceaccount:infra/debug:debug-proxy"

CloudTrail (AWS target account): No successful AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity events; KMS:Decrypt attempts logged for assumed-role/redwood-debug-proxy but denied due to condition aws:SourceAccount mismatch
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: OIDC/WIF audience mismatch. Our token requester uses default GCP audience (iam.googleapis.com) which is not accepted by the WIF trust configured in target AWS accounts that expect audience 'sts.amazonaws.com'.

Secondary finding: When AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity is forced to succeed (using corrected audience), KMS denies Decrypt because the KMS key policy conditions restrict decrypt to the dedicated account's principal or a specific source account; our ephemeral role comes from a different account (redwood-debug), causing aws:SourceAccount condition to fail.

Observed that staging/private account trust mappings diverge: staging has permissive mapping allowing multiple audiences; prod dedicated accounts were locked to only sts.amazonaws.com for security reasons.

Risk assessment: Creating a cross-account trust for debug-proxy increases blast radius if not timebound and constrained to specific principals and keys. Preferred approach is to change token minting in our debug proxy to request the sts-compatible audience and negotiate a short, auditable WIF session, plus add minimal key policy exceptions for the ephemeral role with expiration tags.
Repro playbook attached to this ticket and linked PR with token change: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8041

Post-action: schedule a permissions hardening review to explore making the WIF audience mapping explicit in onboarding to avoid ad-hoc role creations.
